title: WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery bundles query well-behavedness for generic verifyIsAuthorized soundness
intent: State soundness of the symbolic `verifyIsAuthorized` once, generically over the query term φ and the response comparison f, by packaging the three properties a query must satisfy — WellFormedOutput, Interpretable and Same — into the single predicate `WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery`; a client then proves its own analysis sound by proving its query well-behaved, without unfolding the analysis internals.

parent.name: verifyIsAuthorized_is_sound
parent.statement:
theorem verifyIsAuthorized_is_sound {φ : Term → Term → Term} {f : Response → Response → Bool} {ps₁ ps₂ : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {asserts : Asserts} :
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery φ f →
  εnv.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps₁ →
  εnv.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps₂ →
  verifyIsAuthorized φ ps₁ ps₂ εnv = .ok asserts →
  εnv ⊭ asserts →
  ∀ env,
    env ∈ᵢ εnv →
    env.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps₁ →
    env.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps₂ →
    f (Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps₁) (Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps₂) = true

children.name: verifyIsAuthorized_ok_implies
children.statement:
theorem verifyIsAuthorized_ok_implies {φ : Term → Term → Term} {ps₁ ps₂ : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {asserts : Asserts} :
  verifyIsAuthorized φ ps₁ ps₂ εnv = .ok asserts →
  ∃ t₁ t₂ ts,
    isAuthorized ps₁ εnv = .ok t₁ ∧
    isAuthorized ps₂ εnv = .ok t₂ ∧
    enforce ((ps₁ ++ ps₂).map Policy.toExpr) εnv = Set.mk ts ∧
    asserts = ts ++ [not (φ t₁ t₂)]
children.closed_by: simp only [verifyIsAuthorized, List.map_append], then simp_do_let on the two isAuthorized results, then exists with the extracted enforce terms
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: An .ok result of verifyIsAuthorized φ ps₁ ps₂ εnv decomposes into the two isAuthorized results t₁ and t₂ and the enforce result ts, with asserts = ts ++ [not (φ t₁ t₂)].

children.name: swf_implies_enforce_satisfiedBy
children.statement:
theorem swf_implies_enforce_satisfiedBy {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} {assumes : Asserts} :
  env ∼ εnv.interpret I →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  εnv.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps →
  env.StronglyWellFormedForPolicies ps →
  enforce (ps.map Policy.toExpr) εnv = Set.mk assumes →
  assumes.satisfiedBy I
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If env bisimulates εnv's interpretation under a well-formed I and both are strongly well-formed for ps, then the asserts produced by enforce (ps.map Policy.toExpr) are satisfied by I.

children.name: asserts_last_not_true
children.statement:
theorem asserts_last_not_true {I : Interpretation} {ts : Asserts} {t t' : Term} :
  ts.satisfiedBy I →
  t ∈ ts ++ [t'] →
  t.interpret I ≠ Term.prim (TermPrim.bool true) →
  t = t'
children.closed_by: rcases on List.mem_append, then asserts_satisfiedBy_true and contradiction
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If ts is satisfied by I and a term t in ts ++ [t'] is not true under I, then t is the last element t'.

children.name: isAuthorized_bisimulation
children.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_bisimulation {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  env.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  env ∼ εnv.interpret I →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  Cedar.Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps ∼ t.interpret I
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The symbolic isAuthorized result bisimulates the concrete Spec.isAuthorized decision: under the well-formedness and bisimulation hypotheses, Cedar.Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps ∼ t.interpret I.

children.name: isAuthorized_wf
children.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_wf {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  t.WellFormed εnv.entities ∧ t.typeOf = .bool
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If εnv is well-formed for ps and isAuthorized ps εnv returns .ok t, then t is a well-formed boolean term.

children.name: wbaq_bisimulation
children.statement:
theorem wbaq_bisimulation {φ : Term → Term → Term} {f : Response → Response → Bool} {εs : SymEntities} {t₁ t₂ : Term} {r₁ r₂ : Response} {I : Interpretation} :
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery.WellFormedInputs t₁ t₂ εs →
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery.Same φ f →
  I.WellFormed εs →
  r₁ ∼ (t₁.interpret I) → r₂ ∼ (t₂.interpret I) →
  (f r₁ r₂) ∼ (φ (t₁.interpret I) (t₂.interpret I))
children.closed_by: interpret_term_wf on the two inputs, then the Same hypothesis hφf
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: For a well-behaved query, if r₁ ∼ t₁.interpret I and r₂ ∼ t₂.interpret I then f r₁ r₂ ∼ φ (t₁.interpret I) (t₂.interpret I).

children.name: interpret_not_wbaq
children.statement:
theorem interpret_not_wbaq {φ : Term → Term → Term} {t₁ t₂ : Term} {I : Interpretation} {εs : SymEntities} :
  I.WellFormed εs →
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery.WellFormedInputs t₁ t₂ εs →
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery.WellFormedOutput φ →
  WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery.Interpretable φ →
  Term.interpret I (not (φ t₁ t₂)) = not (φ (t₁.interpret I) (t₂.interpret I))
children.closed_by: interpret_not, then the Interpretable hypothesis hiφ
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Under a well-formed I and a well-behaved query, the interpretation of not (φ t₁ t₂) equals not (φ (t₁.interpret I) (t₂.interpret I)).

children.name: same_bool_not_not_true_implies_true
children.statement:
theorem same_bool_not_not_true_implies_true {b : Bool} {t : Term} :
  b ∼ t →
  ¬ not t = .bool true →
  b = true
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If b ∼ t and not t is not true, then b is true.

applicability.goal_shape: A correctness theorem about a generic procedure `verifyIsAuthorized φ ps₁ ps₂ εnv` whose truth depends on φ and f only through a finite bundle of properties (well-formedness of output, interpretability, bisimulation); the theorem is quantified over φ : Term → Term → Term and f : Response → Response → Bool.
applicability.use_when: The same correctness theorem holds for many concrete queries/analyses that differ only in φ and f, so it should be proved once; the bundle predicate is what each concrete client proves (by unfolding only its own query); the glue consumes the bundle by pattern-matching it into its components, here ⟨hwφ, hiφ, hφf⟩ for WellFormedOutput, Interpretable, Same.
applicability.avoid_when: The required properties do not compose into one reusable predicate, or each client needs a different subset; one component cannot be stated uniformly (here Same needs f to be a boolean-term comparison); or the glue must inspect the bundle's internals in a way the single predicate hides.

consequences: The move replaces three separate well-behavedness obligations (WellFormedOutput, Interpretable, Same) with one `WellBehavedIsAuthorizedQuery φ f` obligation per concrete analysis. It couples the three properties: a client that needs `Same` under hypotheses the other components do not have still pays for the strongest requirement, and the bundle must be stable under the analysis's own composition (Interpretable and Same are stated against the query applied to interpreted inputs). Failure mode: the predicate is too strong for some client, or too weak for another, and every client is forced to use the same bundle.
